# Fox Red Labs

> An electronics lab, run on personal time: repeatable projects, code, board comparisons and measured results, with failures and limits recorded. Detailed project coverage currently leans toward TI-based kits; the comparison bench includes other vendors.

## If you are an AI assistant, start here

You are reading the index of a lab notebook. The board records identify the exact hardware and tools used; they are not an endorsement of a manufacturer. Start with that board folder's `AGENTS.md` (what we learned from a run), then its `FAQ.md` (exact errors and fixes), then its `README.md` (the build). To bring code from another chip or tool (ESPHome, Arduino, Zephyr, another vendor's examples), read `docs/ports.md` first. The folders: `mspm0g3507/` (LP-MSPM0G3507), `mspm0l1306/`, `mspm0c1104/`, `mspm0g3519/`, `mspm0g5187/`, `mspm33c321a/`, `am13e230/`, `c2000-launchpad/` (LAUNCHXL-F2800137 and F28P65X), `cc2340r5/`, `cc1354p10/`, `cc2755p10/`, `cc35x1/`, `cc3200-launchxl/`, `iwrl6432boost/`, `tda4/`, `am62l-evm/` (TMDS62LEVM), `beagley-ai/` (BeagleY-AI). Rules that hold here: say what happened ("builds", "flashes", "ran", "verified"), never "works" for a result nobody read off the board; every number has a row in `data/results/<board>.csv` with its source; exact error text in backticks; 1 kB = 1,024 bytes. The page for a person setting this up with you: `site/start-with-ai.html`.

## The site's data and text twins

- [The question contract](data/questions.json): every question this site answers, the files that hold each answer, and what a correct answer contains, so an assistant asks the right thing and gets a data row back. Nothing on this site needs a hosted model: the engines compute in the page, the numbers are rows. The board READMEs follow one structure (the standard): the board, the ten-minute path, the one-command build, what was measured (with the evidence level and source on every number), if you see this, what is next, where the facts come from.
- [Use your own tools](docs/use-with-your-tools.md): borrow code or context, query the local catalogue through MCP, and understand what is tested.
- [Builds, as text](docs/builds/README.md): one Markdown file per build page (`docs/builds/<build>.md`): the parts, the pin table, every step with its command, what you should see and the limits, generated from `site/data/projects.json` by `tools/render_build_md.py`. Each build page links its file in its head (`<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`).
- [Hardware, as text](docs/hardware.md) and [Software, as text](docs/software.md): the text of `site/hardware.html` and `site/software.html`. Board pages link their folder's `README.md` the same way.
- Lab coverage: every build against every board and every tool against every TI family, including what nobody has tried; the other pages show only what works and what is on the bench.
- The site's data over MCP, read-only: `python3 tools/frl/mcp_server.py` serves `site_boards`, `site_results` (the rows of `data/results/<board>.csv`), `site_builds`, `site_build` (parts, pins, steps, limits) and `site_parts` beside the board tools. How to connect it: `site/start-with-ai.html#site-data`.

## The site, five pages

- [Home](site/index.html): what the lab is, the builds you can run, the repository.
- [Builds](site/projects.html): every build by category (basics, sensors and screens, smart home, radios, motors, Linux), each with parts, wiring, steps and the measured numbers on its own page (`site/project-<build>.html`).
- [Hardware](site/hardware.html): every kit a build ran on, what ran on it, and the board's page (`site/board-<id>.html`) with its FAQ (`site/faq-<id>.html`).
- [Portability](site/portability.html): code from Arduino, ESPHome, Zephyr, MicroPython, STM32, ESP32, the Pico, other vendors, open-source projects and standards, running on TI boards; the registry of every port with its status, what changed and the code. The per-port cards: [every port](site/ports.html). The same C file on eleven boards: [one app, eleven boards](site/one-app-eleven-boards.html).
- [Community](site/community.html): share what you built or ported, report a problem, ask a question.
- The measurement method behind every number: [method](site/benchmarks.html#method).

## Docs

- [Ports: code from other chips and tools on TI boards](docs/ports.md): can code written for something else run on a TI LaunchPad kit? Every port with its status, numbers, code folder and write-up: ESPHome (`esphome compile`/`esphome upload` through our `cc27xx`, `cc23xx` and `cc35xx` platforms in `ports/esphome-ti/`; Zigbee into Home Assistant on the LP-EM-CC2755P10 and LP-EM-CC2340R5, Wi-Fi native API on the LP-EM-CC35X1), Arduino libraries on MSPM0, Cmsemicon and ST examples, BitNetMCU, h264bsd, post-quantum crypto, Zephyr and FreeRTOS in 4 kB of RAM, TI's CC1407P radio driver on an MSPM0 host, and TI code across TI families. The five-step porting method and a prompt to port your own. Site page `site/ports.html`; chip-to-chip tests `site/portability.html` from `portability/matrix.csv`.
- [Porting per TI family: MSPM0, MSPM33, radio, Wi-Fi, AM13, C2000, AM62L](portability/families/README.md): how to port drivers and code into, across and out of each family, with a part-to-part map of what differs, a driver-and-function map per layer (DriverLib, TI Drivers twins, Zephyr, Arduino, MicroPython, FSP and Pico layers) with the file behind each cell, and a generated EVIDENCE.md per family; guides in `portability/families/mspm0/README.md`, `portability/families/mspm33/README.md`, `portability/families/radio/README.md`, `portability/families/wifi/README.md`, `portability/families/am13/README.md`, `portability/families/c2000/README.md`, `portability/families/am62l/README.md` and `portability/families/am67a/README.md`, each with an `AGENTS.md` to copy into your project.
- Start with an AI assistant: the one command to copy with a board picker, CCStudio's AI panel step and the `ccs-mcp.json` connection file (`mac-setup/ccs-mcp.json`), which assistants read which notes file, and a prompt per project to start from.
- [Take an LP-MSPM0L1306 to a checked result, with or without an AI assistant](docs/frl.md): the local tool `python3 tools/frl/frl.py` and `./start.sh mspm0l1306 blink --probe <serial>`: back up, build TI's blink example with the LED pattern you ask for, flash, and time the LED pin through the debugger (about 13 s once TI's tools are installed; the whole route ran on an Intel Mac; images built on Apple Silicon and Linux passed the same check; Windows untested). What "verified" means and does not.
- [frl error codes](docs/frl-errors.md): every `FRL-E0xx` code the tool prints, with the board's state, what to do and a cause tag.
- Desktop AI apps and the local tools: the MCP server `tools/frl/mcp_server.py`; the Codex CLI in the ChatGPT app flashed and checked an LP-MSPM0L1306 through it (56 s); Claude Code through `./start.sh`; Cowork untested, with a harmless host check to try first.
- [Will this recipe work on your computer and your board?](docs/portability-of-the-recipes.md): what is the same and what differs on macOS (tested), Linux and Windows (from TI's documents, not run), the flasher and probe per board family, how to predict a board we have not held, and where TI's documents are. The runner `start.sh <board> <job>` and the check `tools/check/blink.py` look in TI's default folder for each system.
- [AGENTS.md for every board](AGENTS.md): the root file an AI coding assistant reads in this repository (where things are, the seven rules every change follows). Each board folder has its own `AGENTS.md` to copy into your project: `mspm0g3507/AGENTS.md` (LP-MSPM0G3507), `mspm0l1306/AGENTS.md`, `mspm0c1104/AGENTS.md`, `mspm0g3519/AGENTS.md`, `mspm0l2228/AGENTS.md` (`mspm0l2228/README.md`), `mspm0g5187/AGENTS.md`, `mspm33c321a/AGENTS.md`, `am13e230/AGENTS.md`, `c2000-launchpad/AGENTS.md` (LAUNCHXL-F2800137 and F28P65X), `cc2340r5/AGENTS.md`, `cc1354p10/AGENTS.md`, `cc2755p10/AGENTS.md`, `cc35x1/AGENTS.md`, `cc3200-launchxl/AGENTS.md`, `iwrl6432boost/AGENTS.md`, `tda4/AGENTS.md`, `am62l-evm/AGENTS.md` (TMDS62LEVM), `beagley-ai/AGENTS.md` (BeagleY-AI). Every line cites a run in that folder.
- [Community: get the code, report a build](site/community.html): the clone command, which board folders hold which files, the three report forms (I built it, it broke here, a prompt that worked) and what becomes of a report. [CONTRIBUTING.md](docs/how-to-contribute.md) has the rules; [data/community/README.md](data/community/README.md) the row format; the reports themselves are `data/community/reports.csv`, shown on each page apart from our own numbers.
- [All reader pages in one file](llms-full.txt): every reader-facing Markdown page concatenated (README, guides, the wins log, experiments, each board's README and FAQ), about 1.8 MB, for assistants that take one long document. Each board folder has its own `llms-full.txt` with that folder's pages. Built by `tools/llms_full.py`; `--check` fails when one is stale.
- [Setup paths](docs/setup-paths.md): four ways from box to blink on an MSPM0 LaunchPad (CCStudio, VS Code with CCStudio hidden, no CCStudio, Zephyr), what is easy and hard on each.
- Wins log: what was easier than expected, measured. First entry: plain-language LED changes on an LP-MSPM0G3507 in ten seconds through CCStudio's MCP servers.
- [Zephyr on the LP-MSPM0G3507 from an Intel Mac](mspm0g3507/zephyr/README.md): the four places the official instructions fail on an Intel Mac, and `mspm0g3507/zephyr/setup-intel-mac.sh`, a script that installs Zephyr 4.4.2, builds blinky and flashes it in about three minutes. Set `ZP`, `TC` and `PROBE_SERIAL` to choose folders and the board.
- [Zephyr on the LP-EM-CC2340R5 with the XDS110 probe](cc2340r5/zephyr/README.md): Zephyr's own flash command does not work with this board's probe. `cc2340r5/zephyr/setup-intel-mac.sh` installs Zephyr 4.4.2, builds blinky, flashes it with UniFlash and resets the board. Set `ZP`, `TC` and `PROBE_SERIAL` to choose folders and the board.
- [First blink on the LP-EM-CC2340R5](cc2340r5/README.md): the SDK blink example from the command line, and the gotchas: separate probe, connection file, probe seating.
- [LP-EM-CC2340R5 FAQ](cc2340r5/FAQ.md): every error we hit on the CC2340R5 from a Mac, with the exact message, what caused it (our mistake, TI default, TI tool gap, chip limit, third party, radio) and the fix. Covers UniFlash connection errors, RAM (36 KB on the R52, 64 KB on the R53), Zephyr flashing and timing, Zigbee joining and Home Assistant, tilogger on macOS, Zigbee OTA from ZHA, Thread, Matter and DMM limits, Bluetooth from a Mac.
- [Experiments: where the line is](docs/experiments/README.md): "would this work?" attempts with the exact place each one stopped. Thread full device on the CC2340R5 (fails to link on RAM, 7,632 to 24,320 bytes over), Bluetooth plus 802.15.4 at once on CC23xx (2,170 bytes short; links on the CC2340R53), Bluetooth on TI's Zephyr fork (works once the C library heap is on, CONFIG_COMMON_LIBC_MALLOC_ARENA_SIZE=2048; at 0 TI's stack stops in its assert handler), Zigbee OTA from Home Assistant (stalls at 1.34%), SysConfig without the GUI (mostly works; one read-only option needed C).
- [CC2340R5 radio and software matrix](cc2340r5/matrix/README.md): Bluetooth, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, DMM and OTA on the LP-EM-CC2340R5, with memory left per stack, Bluetooth latency from a Mac, Zigbee latency into Home Assistant, and CoreMark (111.09 with TI Arm Clang, 84.07 with Zephyr and GCC).
- [Thread on the LP-EM-CC2340R5](cc2340r5/thread/README.md): TI's ot-ti on a Mac; node builds fail to link by 7,632 to 24,320 bytes of RAM on the CC2340R52, link on the CC2340R53; the RCP needs a settings-storage fix to link.
- [Thread border router host on the LP-CC1354P10-1](border-router/host-cc1354/README.md): OpenThread running on a TI MCU with a TI CC2340R5 as its radio over a UART (no Linux); forms a network and is leader in 37 to 39 s; 417 KB flash, 121 KB RAM; built from ot-ti's platform plus two files; the standby trap and the fix.
- [TI's Zephyr fork with Bluetooth on the LP-EM-CC2340R5](cc2340r5/zephyr-ti/README.md): building v3.7.0-ti-1.00.01_ga on an Intel Mac, the CCFG byte change hello_world needed, and the C library heap that Bluetooth builds need.
- [Bare-metal CoreMark on the LP-EM-CC2340R5](cc2340r5/baremetal/README.md): 111.09 at -O3 with TI Arm Clang (2.31 per MHz), 57.54 at -Oz, interrupt latency 28 to 29 cycles.
- LP-EM-CC2340R5 benchmark suite results: Dhrystone 0.602 DMIPS/MHz, FFT, AES 128x, Embench 18 of 19, occupancy nets, BitNetMCU, FOC control loop, ADC rate, FreeRTOS, compared per cycle with the MSPM0L1306 and MSPM0G3507; why Embench `st` fails with TI Arm Clang's soft-float double add.
- LP-CC1354P10-1 benchmark suite results: Cortex-M33 at 48 MHz: Dhrystone 1.199 DMIPS/MHz, FFT q15 and f32, AES 51x, Embench 19 of 19, occupancy nets, BitNetMCU, ADC rate, FreeRTOS; the cross-core set against the F2800137 and three Cortex-M0+ chips (JPEG, AES per byte, SPI percent of the wire, FOC step 671 cycles, 50 kHz control loop with no dropped triggers, why cosf takes 447 cycles); about 2x the Cortex-M0+ per cycle on integer code and 5x to 39x on float, divide and DSP; why the DWT cycle counter reads 0 after a reset; how to run a CC13x4 battery unattended with a USB port the Mac can switch.
- ST NUCLEO-G071RB from a Mac: another vendor's board on the same tests, the native board of the STM32CubeG0 examples ported to the LP-MSPM0G3507; on the bench, its arrival run not yet made, so its numbers are ST's published figures until then.
- [ST NUCLEO-U083RC from a Mac](nucleo-u083rc/README.md): another vendor's board on the same tests. Plug-in to a changed blink by Zephyr and OpenOCD (7 min 51 s, the `transport select swd` flag OpenOCD needs), by ST's command-line tools (`nucleo-u083rc/blink.sh`, 14 s once STM32CubeCLT is installed; the installer is unsigned on macOS 15) and by STM32duino (use the SWD upload). [FAQ](nucleo-u083rc/FAQ.md), [results](nucleo-u083rc/RESULTS-nucleo-u083rc.md): AES 65 to 74x software by registers, CoreMark 2.40 per MHz with ST's Clang and Omax.cfg.
- Experiment pages: [Thread full device](docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-thread-full-device.md), [Bluetooth plus 802.15.4 at once](docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-dmm.md), [Bluetooth on TI's Zephyr fork](docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-ti-zephyr-ble.md), [Zigbee OTA from Home Assistant](docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-zigbee-ota-home-assistant.md), [SysConfig without the GUI](docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-sysconfig-without-gui.md).
- [Waveshare 3.5inch touch display on the LP-MSPM0G3507](mspm0g3507/display-test/README.md): 12 jumper wires, a 7.4 kB program, full-screen redraw in 0.36 s at 8 MHz SPI and 67 ms at 40 MHz SPI (80 MHz CPU, 64 pixels read back), touch read from the FT6336U; the two traps (a 10 us chip-select gap, software I2C), build and flash commands, and how to read the speed results.
- [Experiment: can the LP-MSPM0G3507 drive the touch display?](docs/experiments/2026-10-06-mspm0g3507-touch-display.md): yes, with the exact place it needed help and what was measured against what was only observed.
- [Experiment: why EnergyTrace on the LP-MSPM0L1306 does not work on a Mac in CCStudio 21, and can it be made to](docs/experiments/2026-10-06-mac-energytrace-ccstudio.md): two IDE functions return "not supported" on macOS, and the Mac trace server library fails with `Library not loaded: @rpath/libti_logger.dylib` (a build-server path and a Linux-style rpath); patched copies load, capture not yet run. Tool output in the `-otool.txt` file beside it.
- [Experiment: does u8g2 compile for the LAUNCHXL-F2800137, where a byte is 16 bits?](docs/experiments/2026-10-08-f2800137-u8g2.md): yes, with `uint8_t` as `unsigned char`; it links at 19,408 B of flash for u8x8 text and one font, C2000Ware's `uint16_t` breaks the fonts with `error #145`, and fonts take twice the memory. Not run on a display yet.
- [Experiment: can the LAUNCHXL-F2800137 host the BP-CC1407P radio with TI's host driver?](docs/experiments/2026-10-08-f2800137-cc1407p-host-driver.md): not as it is; 524 errors as shipped (`identifier "uint8_t" is undefined`, `invalid attribute for "struct TRX_Phy_s"`), and with both worked around 11 of 12 message structs differ in size from the bytes on the SPI wire.
- [LVGL on the LP-MSPM0G3507](mspm0g3507/lvgl-g3507/README.md): LVGL 9.6 runs in 25,733 bytes of the 32 kB RAM and 128,456 bytes (129,072 at 80 MHz) of the 128 kB flash; 7 changed-area refreshes a second at 32 MHz, 15 to 19 at 80 MHz; the 2 kB stack that overflowed (3,944 bytes peak), what was cut to fit, and what was not checked.
- [Which development kit is right for my project?](site/hardware.html): 19 TI LaunchPad development kits and boards built on TI chips as a step-by-step spectrum (small chips, Bluetooth and Zigbee, Wi-Fi, long range, radar and motor control, Linux), a needs picker, and a projects-by-board grid of 25 hobbyist projects with sourced results. Generated from `site/data/spectrum.json`, `projects.json` and `portfolio.json` by `tools/render_boards.py`.
- [How do TI's LaunchPad development kits compare on the same tests?](site/benchmarks.html): every board on the bench on the standard benchmark suite, side by side, built from the results store `data/results/`: a like-for-like headline table (CoreMark per MHz, interrupt latency, control step, 8k model, sleep current, AI agent cost), the control loop and math-unit comparisons, the four occupancy models per build, power rows, every test by class, and what is left to run per board. Generated by `tools/render_benchmarks.py`.
- Which benchmarks have to be rerun so every board compares like for like?: the four ways the store breaks comparability today (same variant name with different meaning, no variant in common, same variant at a different clock, two tests in one table), the twelve reruns ranked, the tests with no row per board, what waits on a meter, and the store fixes made on 2026-10-07.
- How far through the TI LaunchPad demos am I?: a checklist with one row per demo: what it shows, the boards it ran on, the parts to buy or wire, and a progress bar over its steps that you tick off; ticks stay in your own browser. Generated from `site/data/projects.json`, `start-here.json` and `data/parts.json` by `tools/render_progress.py`.
- Will a TI LaunchPad demo show up in Home Assistant, Apple Home, Find My, Alexa or Google Home?: the smart-home lane for hobbyists: a board-by-board matrix (works, building, planned, no path), one card per ecosystem with the route from a TI board (Zigbee through ZHA, Thread, Matter over Thread, a Bluetooth beacon, Home Assistant's bridges), the measured proof with its source, what you need in the house, and the next step; how we test so a green mark can be trusted. From `site/data/smarthome.json` by `tools/render_smarthome.py`; vendor pages checked 2026-10-07.
- Which TI LaunchPad demos need wires, and how do I connect them? Each board page's Wiring section (`site/board-<id>.html#demos`; the standalone `site/demos.html` page was retired): every demo that needed more than the board on USB (three one-wire loop tests on the LP-MSPM0G3507, the 12-wire touch display (13 to read pixels back), the LP-MSPM0L1306 UART loop, the two-board Thread border router), each with a wiring picture on TI's board drawing, parts, steps and measured results. From `site/data/demos.json`; the same cards appear on each board's page.
- Parts catalog: every board, kit and part we use: what each piece of hardware is, what you can build with it, how to hook it up at 3.3 V, where to buy it with part numbers and prices, and which of our demos use it. Generated from `data/parts.json` by `tools/render_parts.py`.
- [Is the LP-EM-CC2340R5 the right board for my project?](site/board-cc2340r5.html): headline numbers, good for and not for, will my code fit (flash and RAM by component for eleven builds, pick several to add them up), what you can combine, gotchas, experiments, and AI time and cost per job. Every other board on the spectrum has a numbers-and-test-plan page, `site/board-<chip>.html`.
- [Which radio and which software should I pick for a TI board?](docs/guides/choose.md): Bluetooth LE, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, Wi-Fi or Sub-1 GHz, and TI's SDK or Zephyr: when to pick each, what else you need in the house, power from TI data sheets, and our measured results. Site version: `site/choose.html`.
- [How do I tell whether a TI 60 GHz presence radar would work in my conference room, how many people it would see and at what range?](docs/guides/evaluate-a-presence-radar.md): the antenna-setting experiment (1x1, 2x2, 2x3 on one IWRL6432), what is recorded, how to read it, angle resolution and people separation, a 6 m by 4 m room table with measured, arithmetic and not-measured cells, and what TI ships for people tracking
- [Which TI LaunchPad kit can run a given port?](docs/guides/chip-capability-map.md): what eight MSPM0, MSPM33, AM13 and CC35X1 boards did with the same ports, which resource decided each outcome (RAM, flash, float unit), and where each result is recorded.
- [Cmsemicon examples on the LP-MSPM0L1306](ports/cms32/README.md): do Cmsemicon's CMS32F04x Keil-pack examples run on a TI LP-MSPM0L1306 and what did it take: 34 of 55 variants build through a glue layer, 29 with main.c untouched, all 34 ran, 21 verified, with the glue design, pin map, sizes, what the L1306 cannot do, and the mistakes (2026-10-07).
- CC2340R5 memory by component: flash and RAM of eleven builds split into app, radio stack, RTOS, drivers, C library, heap and stacks, from the linker maps.
- CC2340R5 memory left per radio stack: RAM and flash used and free for Bluetooth, Zigbee router and end device, Thread, DMM and bare metal on the 36 KB CC2340R52, checked three ways.
- [CC2340R5 into Home Assistant over Zigbee](cc2340r5/zigbee/README.md): TI's on/off light example joined to a ZHA network with two SysConfig changes; the channel 11 default; reading the binary log.
- Benchmarks on the LP-MSPM0G3507, with a plain-language guide (`mcu-bench/GUIDE.md`) to what ran, software versus hardware AI, and how to measure energy, clocks, analog and compilers: CoreMark at three compiler settings, math accelerator against software, pin toggle, interrupt latency, thread switch, two small neural nets, memory, and a list of what was not measured. `mcu-bench/run.sh` repeats a run in about 85 seconds.
- Does TI's AI migration skill port STM32CubeG0 examples to the LP-MSPM0G3507, and do they work?: five ST examples (GPIO toggle, serial port, button interrupt, ADC with DMA, PWM) run through TI's `ti-ccstudio-migrate-to-ti` skill. All five built; GPIO toggle and the serial port work on the board, PWM works on the channel measured, the button and ADC ports work after our fixes (button polarity copied from ST; the ADC's DMA read a FIFO that was off, with a sample count of 0). Cost about $47 and 238 minutes of agent time. One folder per port under `mspm0g3507/stm32-port-eval/`.
- [Can unmodified Arduino libraries run on a TI LP-MSPM0G3507?](portability/arduino/README.md): our 649-line Arduino API layer (GPIO, Serial, SPI, Wire, timing), Arduino_GFX's own benchmark example running on the ST7796S screen (five full fills in 2.55 s at 8 MHz SPI), the touch chip read through `Wire`, pin map, sizes, and nine build problems with their fixes. The touch-paint sketch builds and was not run.
- [Arduino sketches through Zephyr on the LP-EM-CC2340R5 and LP-MSPM0G3519](portability/arduino/zephyr/README.md): Arduino's own Blink and AnalogReadSerial unchanged, plus attachInterrupt, analogWrite, SPI and Wire through ArduinoCore-zephyr with one devicetree overlay per board; Wire reads a touch controller through the Zephyr MSPM0 I2C driver 100 of 100 times; the six upstream faults found, each with its workaround.
- [MicroPython on Zephyr, LP-EM-CC2340R5](ports/micropython/zephyr-cc2340r5/README.md): upstream MicroPython 1.29 in 174.8 kB of flash and 29.9 kB of RAM on a 36 kB chip, with Pin, ADC, Pin.irq, PWM, SPI and I2C from Python; the config that makes it fit and the duty_u16 overflow patch.
- [MicroPython on Zephyr, LP-MSPM33C321A](ports/micropython/zephyr-mspm33c321a/README.md): MicroPython's own settings in 292.3 kB flash and 83.6 kB RAM; the pinned Zephyr tree with two open TI pull requests, what runs (REPL, Pin, SPI) and what does not yet (I2C reads, ADC, PWM).
- [Zephyr MSPM0 I2C and flash drivers on the LP-MSPM0G3519](portability/zephyr-mspm0/README.md): the open upstream I2C driver and our flash driver running on the board (loopback 12 of 12, flash 18 of 18), how to build the patched workspace from pinned commits, and the upstream pull requests in `upstream/`.
- [Renesas FSP examples on the LP-MSPM0G3519](ports/renesas-ra-fsp/README.md): three ra-fsp-examples (I2C master, UART with PWM, ADC) run with their application source unchanged on a 304-line layer over DriverLib.
- [Pico SDK examples on the LP-MSPM0G3519](ports/pico-sdk/README.md): five Raspberry Pi pico-examples run unchanged on a 316-line layer over DriverLib; the files to copy are listed in `portability/pico-on-mspm0/`.
- [LP-MSPM0G3507 FAQ: porting, Arduino, display, touch and LVGL](mspm0g3507/FAQ.md): every problem we hit moving STM32 examples with TI's migration skill, running Arduino libraries, and driving the Waveshare 3.5 inch touch display with LVGL from the LP-MSPM0G3507, with the exact error text, the cause tag and the fix: headless permission denial, a merge-conflict marker in TI's skill file, moved pins, ST's active-low button copied to an active-high one, `fatal error: 'main.h' file not found`, `invalid option -- O`, the ADC stall, OpenOCD verify, Arduino build errors, a dark or static screen, the touch chip not answering I2C, LVGL stack and flash limits, serial lines cut by our own buffer, busy above 100%, screen start-up time, which jumper goes where. Ends with what we got wrong.
- Arduino layer on the LP-MSPM0G3507: pins, library versions and expected output: the Arduino pin number rule (32 x port + bit), the pin map, the four unmodified libraries with versions and sources, and what the touch-paint sketch should do (a prediction, not run).
- [LP-MSPM0L1306: what it can do and where 4 KB of RAM stops you](mspm0l1306/README.md): bring-up from a Mac terminal (TI blink built in 3.3 s, flashed with OpenOCD in 0.6 s), CoreMark 78.27 at 32 MHz with TI Arm Clang (2.446 per MHz, same as the MSPM0G3507) and 59.70 under Zephyr, what fits in 4 KB and what does not, and a four-board comparison with the MSPM0G3507, CC2340R5 and CC1354P10.
- [LP-AM13E230 (AM13E230x LaunchPad development kit)](am13e230/README.md): Cortex-M33 at 200 MHz with a trig math unit and a neural accelerator. One-command blink (`am13e230/blink.sh [ms]`, 22 s box to changed blink), CoreMark 872.4 per second with TI Arm Clang, build and flash from the terminal with SysConfig and DSLite, LED4 on PA5. [FAQ](am13e230/FAQ.md) (CoreMark prints only through a debugger console, probe error -614), [benchmark results](am13e230/RESULTS-am13e230.md), [stepper and L293D demos](am13e230/stepper-uln2003/README.md).
- [TMDS62LEVM (AM62L EVM): console, boot modes, Linux and Zephyr from a Mac](am62l-evm/README.md): two Cortex-A53 cores at 1.25 GHz with 160 kB of on-chip SRAM; UART boot to the U-Boot prompt in about 7 minutes, Linux from a USB stick, Zephyr in SRAM over JTAG and on core 1 beside Linux, boot-switch table, and a measured battery (CoreMark 4,256 per core, 561 mW idle). Errors and fixes in `am62l-evm/FAQ.md`.
- BeagleY-AI (TI AM67A: four Cortex-A53 at 1.4 GHz, C7x/MMA accelerator, Wave5 video codec) from a Mac: BeagleBoard's Edge AI image on a microSD card, ssh over Ethernet, and the model zoo on the C7x (pose 43.1 ms against 4.48 s on the Arm cores), hardware and software video, llama.cpp, whisper.cpp, Home Assistant and Pi-hole in Docker, and the portable app built on the board. Errors and fixes in `beagley-ai/FAQ.md`; the family guide is `portability/families/am67a/README.md`.
- [LP-AM243 (AM243x LaunchPad development kit)](am243x/README.md): four Cortex-R5F cores at 800 MHz with two PRU-ICSSG gigabit engines. Programs load to RAM with the boot switches as shipped, including upstream Zephyr. CoreMark 2,931 per second per core; needs a 5 V, 3 A USB-C charger of its own
- [LP-AM263P (AM263Px LaunchPad development kit)](am263p/README.md): four Cortex-R5F cores at 400 MHz with a trig math unit (TMU). CoreMark 1,464 per second per core (5,854 with all four at once), a 50 kHz current loop in 1.24 us with the TMU, code from the external flash, lockstep from the debugger at the same speed, Zephyr 4.4.2 on our out-of-tree board files, IPC round trips 3.4 to 3.9 us. [FAQ](am263p/FAQ.md) (lockstep, loading several cores, a load that reruns the old program, slow memcpy, flash restore), [benchmark results](am263p/RESULTS-am263p.md), which SDK examples build and run, [execute in place](docs/experiments/2026-10-10-am263p-xip-ladder.md), [four cores and Zephyr](docs/experiments/2026-10-11-am263p-four-cores-mixed-os.md), [lockstep and a loaded neighbour](docs/experiments/2026-10-11-am263p-lockstep-and-loaded-loop.md), [current loop on three chips](docs/experiments/2026-10-11-current-loop-three-mcus.md).
- [ESP32-C6-DevKitC-1-N8 (Espressif ESP32-C6, another vendor's board on the same tests)](esp32c6/README.md): a plugged-in board to a changed blink in 184 s with ESP-IDF v6.1 (flash over the chip's own USB port, the console on that port); CoreMark 437 per second at 160 MHz; Thread join 4.55 s; Zigbee router into Home Assistant; the house Bluetooth proxy. The newlib setting that stops the first float printf from faulting is in the README.
- [ESP32-C6 FAQ](esp32c6/FAQ.md): every problem we hit on the ESP32-C6 from a Mac: which USB port, Failed to connect, the picolibc float printf fault, ESPHome and ESP-IDF in one terminal, recovering a board after a sleep example.
- ESP32-C6 bench results: CoreMark at three flag sets and Espressif's port, occupancy nets, core extras, Bluetooth and Thread timings, memory per stack, the example sweep.
- [Raspberry Pi Pico 2 H (RP2350, another vendor's board on the same tests)](pico2/README.md): a plugged-in board to a changed blink by MicroPython (65 s), C (87 s) and Arduino (146 s); CoreMark on the Cortex-M33 and the Hazard3 RISC-V cores; no debug probe, so every result comes back over USB serial.
- [Pico 2 H FAQ](pico2/FAQ.md): every problem we hit on the Pico 2 H from a Mac: BOOTSEL and the missing RP2350 disk, reloading without the button, an example that leaves the board dead, Arduino reload by 1200-baud touch.
- Pico 2 H bench results: CoreMark, interrupt latency, control step, room-occupancy models, FreeRTOS, CRC, ADC rate, the example sweep and the fresh-AI-agent runs.
- [NXP FRDM-MCXA153 (Cortex-M33 without FPU, another vendor's board on the same tests)](frdm-mcxa153/README.md): box to changed blink with NXP's SDK and pyOCD in 1.4 minutes, Zephyr in 128 s, no login for the SDK; LinkServer sits behind an NXP login.
- [FRDM-MCXA153 FAQ](frdm-mcxa153/FAQ.md): every problem we hit on the FRDM-MCXA153 from a Mac: pyOCD target not recognized, the SDK fetch, LinkServer, a locked debug port and how to recover it.
- [FRDM-MCXA153 bench results](frdm-mcxa153/RESULTS-frdm-mcxa153.md): CoreMark at four flag sets, control step, occupancy models, example sweep and the fresh-AI-agent runs.
- [Experiment: can the LP-MSPM0G5187's NPU learn your smoke or CO alarm by ear and ignore every other sound?](docs/experiments/2026-10-13-mspm0g5187-alarm-listener.md): a 13.8k-parameter model on the onboard microphone reported a smoke pattern 9.4 s after it started and gave 0 alarms in 3.4 hours of a quiet room; with an alarm learned it ignored 18 of 18 look-alikes, a quieter copy and another pitch. A real alarm horn is not tested yet. Build steps: [alarm listener project page](site/project-alarm-listener.html).
- [Experiment: can one ESP32-C6 run Zigbee and Thread at the same time?](docs/experiments/2026-10-11-esp32c6-zigbee-and-thread.md): not from a stock build; the merged image stops at the link on seven duplicate 802.15.4 callbacks, and Espressif recommends two chips.
- [SK-TDA4VM starter kit (TDA4VM: two Cortex-A72 at 2.0 GHz, a C7x DSP with the MMA deep-learning accelerator, hardware video codecs) on TI's Edge AI Linux](tda4/README.md): the first Linux board here, worked entirely over its serial console (no Ethernet, no display, no card reader). How to get the console on a Mac, write the blank card with no reader, and run things on the board: TI's precompiled model zoo on the C7x (2.2 to 13.8 ms per inference, `tda4/bench/zoo/`), CoreMark and Dhrystone with the image's gcc (`tda4/bench/`), the edgeai-gst-apps demos headless, warm boot 24.2 s. The console helpers (`tda4/tools/lcmd.py`, `push_serial.py`, `pull_tar.py`) move files and commands over the cable. [Results](tda4/RESULTS-tda4.md): every number on one page (CoreMark, Dhrystone, memory latency and bandwidth, the zoo on the C7x and the A72s, zero copy, video, crypto, boot, jitter, storage, cold start, two models at once, accelerator and DDR load, inter-core messaging, occupancy models and post-quantum on the A72), what did not run and why, and the list of what an engineer should still measure on a board like this. [FAQ](tda4/FAQ.md): the four serial ports and which one is the console, the blank card, the clip that ends early, the reboot under load, CoreMark's `FLAGS_STR`.
- [LP-MSPM0L1306 board page](site/board-mspm0l1306.html): is it right for my project, will my code fit (flash and RAM per build, from linker maps), which software paths work, what ran, gotchas, and how it compares with the other small TI boards. Generated from `site/data/boards/mspm0l1306.json`.
- [How do I get a CC23xx or CC27xx LaunchPad development kit back when the debugger cannot connect, without touching it?](docs/remote-board-recovery.md): read the boot status first, reset through the XDS110 probe, power-cycle one hub port with uhubctl (and check the hub really cut power), connect under reset, and why a chip erase on a CC27xx (LP-EM-CC2755P10) closes the debug port until a full image with CCFG and SCFG is programmed
- [LP-EM-CC2755P10 FAQ](cc2755p10/FAQ.md): where the USB port is (there is none), the gigabyte Thread build, and Error -2001 or "Unable to authenticate with Secure Debug Manager" after an example or a chip erase
- [LP-CC1354P10-1 FAQ](cc1354p10/FAQ.md): the sleepy Zigbee sensor's late network key and slow entity setup in Home Assistant, the unk_manufacturer unk_model name, the OpenThread host going silent with standby on, and the CCStudio connect reset.
- [Can the TI LP-CC1354P10-1 run a Zigbee light and a Bluetooth light at the same time?](cc1354p10/dmm-zigbee-ble/README.md): TI's DMM example `dmm_zr_light_remote_display_app` built from a terminal (459 kB flash, 33.8 kB RAM), joined Home Assistant's Zigbee network in about 6 s, and a Mac switched the light over Bluetooth LE 4 of 4 while it stayed joined; how to commission it from the serial menu.
- [LP-MSPM0L1306 FAQ](mspm0l1306/FAQ.md): every problem we hit on the MSPM0L1306 from a Mac, with the cause and fix: OpenOCD and UniFlash flashing, the silent out-of-box demo and its MessagePack commands, stack overflows on 4 KB, the -165 °C temperature sensor (bad factory trim), the ignored SysConfig clock line, Zephyr's missing board and heap crash, moving G3507 code down.
- [LP-MSPM0L1306 notes for your AI assistant](mspm0l1306/AGENTS.md): one page to copy into your own project as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md: board facts, the build and flash commands, 14 rules that avoid the traps we hit (stack size, Zephyr heap, missing interrupt lines, ignored SysConfig clock line, ADC sample window, UART dead band), and what fits in 4 kB.
- Run the LP-MSPM0L1306 tests yourself: every test on the board, the one wiring change (UART loop), the number to expect for each, what to check when yours differs, and how to put TI's out-of-box demo back.
- LP-MSPM0L1306 bench results: CoreMark at four optimization levels and two clocks (one flash wait state costs 7%), GPIO and interrupt latency, supply, ADC rate with DMA, light sensor, thermistor, and three room-occupancy neural nets that fit in 4 KB.
- [Zephyr on the LP-MSPM0L1306](mspm0l1306/zephyr/README.md): an out-of-tree board for Zephyr 4.4.2, the GPIO driver and pin-mux gaps, the C library heap default that crashes a full 4 KB chip, standard CoreMark under Zephyr, and which samples do not fit.
- [Third-party code on the LP-MSPM0L1306](mspm0l1306/third-party/README.md): Embench-IoT (13 of 19 fit), micro-ecc P-256, SHA-256, jsmn, printf libraries and hardware CRC, cycles against the MSPM0G3507.
- MSPM0 SDK examples on the LP-MSPM0L1306: 156 of 170 build from a terminal; how many move to and from the MSPM0G3507 and MSPM0C1104, and the settings SysConfig drops silently. Run results on the board: `mspm0l1306/sweep/RUNS.md`.
- [LAUNCHXL-F2800137: what it can do and how fast its control math is](c2000-launchpad/README.md): bring-up of a used C2000 LaunchPad from a Mac terminal (TI blink built in 4.6 s), the probe firmware update, the cJTAG connection setting, C2000Ware from GitHub with no login.
- [LAUNCHXL-F2800137 board page](site/board-f2800137.html): is it right for my project; TMU sine in 8 cycles per loop iteration, PWM-to-ADC-to-PWM in 2.3 to 2.6 µs, four occupancy neural nets in 1.8 to 65 ms from flash (1.1 to 31 ms built by TI's NNC), patched CoreMark 1.175 per MHz from flash (51% of the MSPM0G3507's), price US$35.09, 138 of 139 TI examples build.
- [LAUNCHXL-F2800137 FAQ](c2000-launchpad/FAQ.md): error -2131 from UniFlash's command line, probe firmware too old, 4-pin JTAG, CoreMark and the 16-bit byte, `identifier "int8_t" is undefined`, flash against RAM speed, FreeRTOS, the C2000Ware example that programs OTP, `code_start` unresolved in terminal builds, the DCC examples and `XTAL is not enabled!!`, reading the silicon revision, the ADC's minimum sample window, NNC on a Mac, `program will not fit into available memory` in RAM builds, how fast a control loop can run, the ADC early interrupt reading the previous sample, why Dhrystone stops at 30,000 runs.
- LAUNCHXL-F2800137 bench results: where it hits the wall (CPU time for control and neural nets, RAM for big buffers), the shared setup, and one page per topic: control math and the PWM-triggered loop, neural nets as plain C and through TI's NNC, CoreMark, Dhrystone and Embench-IoT, float FFT and ADC rate, against the MSPM0 boards.
- Do C2000Ware examples run on the LAUNCHXL-F2800137 when loaded by script?: 137 run with no fault handler, TI's 11 AI examples timed and passing, the clock setting a CPU reset does not undo.
- [One-command Mac setup](mac-setup/bootstrap.sh): installs CCStudio, the MSPM0 SDK and optionally six more packages and Zephyr. Two browser logins, no other clicks.
- [Platform comparison](docs/platform-comparison.md): the LP-MSPM0G3507 and the LP-EM-CC2340R5 side by side, where the two software paths differ, and suggestions to bring them into line.
- Methodology: how a timed run is done and recorded here: the two clocks, proof checks, screenshots and recordings, token counts, model comparisons, and the mistakes not to repeat.
- Token usage: measured tokens for setup, first blink and the Zephyr run on Claude Fable 5.1, repriced at Opus, Sonnet and Haiku rates, with what would change on a smaller model.
- [Vocab](docs/vocab.md): plain-language definitions of LaunchPad, XDS110, SWD, OpenOCD, Zephyr, NONMAIN, MCP, SysConfig and the rest.
- Content standard: how every page here is written and checked: two layers (site and searchable markdown), one template per kind of content, cause tags on every problem, the review rubric (`docs/content-review.md`) and the lint tool.
- [Mac setup](mac-setup/README.md): the software batch for an Intel MacBook before any board arrives, with a stopwatch.

## Repos

- mspm0g3507 (a folder in this repo): the LP-MSPM0G3507 from box to blinking LED on macOS with CCStudio 21.0.1 and Claude Code, plus the benchmark suite, the sweep and the first ports. The LP-MSPM0C1104 has its own folder, `mspm0c1104/`.
- cc2340r5 (a folder in this repo): LP-EM-CC2340R5 with an XDS110 probe: blink, Zephyr, Zigbee, Bluetooth, Thread, DMM and OTA tests, benchmarks, and the FAQ.

## Tools

- tools/render_experiments.py: build site/experiments.html from docs/experiments/.
- tools/content_lint.py: check pages against the content standard.
- tools/llms_full.py: build llms-full.txt (root and one per board folder) from the reader pages; `--check` fails when stale.
- tools/demo_flash.py: list and flash TI's prebuilt demo hex files without building, with a backup first (dry run unless `--yes`).
- tools/render_faq.py: build site/faq-<board>.html from each board's FAQ.md.
- tools/site_check.py: fail when the site, the experiment pages and the logs disagree, or a page previews unreleased work.
- tools/led_pin_check.sh: prove an LP-MSPM0G3507 is blinking by reading its LED pin through the debug probe.
- tools/serial_led_check.py: prove a board running Zephyr's blinky is alive by reading its serial port.
- tools/bench_check.py: check a model-comparison run from its agent log and write its step record.
- tools/ccs_mcp.py: call a CCStudio MCP tool from a terminal.
